titulo: Money here: the card is the one with a law behind it
subtitulo: Taking the card is an obligation tied to the trade's activity code, cash stops at five hundred, and a single-machine island now costs nothing to withdraw from
cena: A till in a village square, a card in your hand, and a cash machine forty metres away that you are about to need — or not.
frasePiso: Δέχεστε κάρτα; asked in the doorway costs you nothing and settles the whole meal.
decisao: decidir na porta como vou pagar e quanto tiro no caixa — cartão é obrigação legal por ΚΑΔ, espécie tem teto de €500 e a taxa de saque tem teto nacional de €1,50 — em vez de descobrir a condição com a conta na mão e tratar «μόνο μετρητά» como golpe

fatosDatados.afirmacao: In Greece the duty is to ACCEPT card payment, not merely to own a terminal. Article 65 of law 4446/2016 imposes acceptance of card payment means, and article 66 requires the business to inform the consumer visibly at the entrance and at the till. The scope runs by ΚΑΔ, the activity code of the trade: the list was replaced by joint ministerial decision 119899/2023, ΦΕΚ Β΄7115 of 18.12.2023, which added 35 further codes, among them open-air markets, food retail and kiosks. That makes refusing a card unlawful far more often here than in Italy or France. Two honest limits: coverage is not universal, because the legal criterion remains the ΚΑΔ list rather than «all commerce», and the domestic instant-payment scheme IRIS, compulsory across retail since 01.11.2025, runs on Greek bank accounts and is normally out of reach for a foreign visitor.
fatosDatados.fonte: Art. 65 do ν.4446/2016, «Υποχρέωση αποδοχής μέσων πληρωμής με κάρτα», obriga por ΚΑΔ (código de atividade); o art. 66 obriga a informar o consumidor de forma visível na entrada e no caixa. A lista de ΚΑΔ foi substituída pela ΚΥΑ 119899/2023, ΦΕΚ Β΄7115/18.12.2023, que estendeu a mais 35 ΚΑΔ — feiras livres, varejo alimentar, bancas. ⚠️ A cobertura NÃO é universal: o critério legal continua sendo a lista de ΚΑΔ. IRIS é doméstico e o turista estrangeiro normalmente não consegue usar.

fatosDatados.afirmacao: Cash to a business has a ceiling of 500 euros. Article 69 §2 of law 4446/2016 set that figure, cutting the previous 1 500 euros: an invoice of 500 euros or more has to be settled by card, transfer or another electronic means. Property is a separate regime altogether — article 3 of law 5073/2023 requires payment exclusively through banking channels, with no cash allowance at all, on pain of nullity.
fatosDatados.fonte: Teto de espécie: €500 para consumidor→empresa — art. 69 §2 do ν.4446/2016, que reduziu o limite anterior de €1.500. Fatura de valor igual ou superior a €500 tem de ser paga por cartão, transferência ou meio eletrônico. Imóveis são caso à parte: o art. 3 do ν.5073/2023 exige pagamento exclusivamente por meio bancário, sem franquia em numerário, sob pena de nulidade de pleno direito. ⚠️ A multa de €100 ao emitente vem de fonte secundária — não afirmar o valor.

fatosDatados.afirmacao: Withdrawal fees were capped by article 48 of law 5167/2024, amended on 25.07.2025 and in force since 11.08.2025. It removes the commission on a withdrawal made on the issuing bank's own network; it takes the fee to zero in a municipal community served by a single cash machine; and it fixes a national ceiling of 1.50 euros per withdrawal charged by an independent operator. The practical consequence for a small island or a mountain village is direct: you are not at the mercy of whatever figure the machine announces.
fatosDatados.fonte: ACHADO NOVO E ÚTIL PARA ILHA — taxa de saque. O art. 48 do ν.5167/2024, alterado em 25.07.2025 e vigente desde 11.08.2025: elimina comissão em saque na rede do próprio banco emissor, zera a tarifa em comunidade municipal onde opera um ÚNICO ATM, e fixa teto nacional de €1,50 por saque cobrado por operador independente.

fatosDatados.afirmacao: Tipping exists here and is institutionally recognised, but no percentage is published anywhere. What exists is a tax rule: law 5162/2024 exempts tips of up to 300 euros a month per worker from income tax, for amounts paid from 01.11.2024, and exempts the whole of them from social contributions. That confirms the practice and confirms nothing about how much. No research body, sector federation or statistical office publishes a figure for Greece, so any percentage you have read came from a blog.
fatosDatados.fonte: Gorjeta tem fonte institucional, mas só para o tratamento FISCAL: o ν.5162/2024 isenta de imposto gorjetas até €300/mês por trabalhador, para valores pagos a partir de 01.11.2024, e isenta de contribuição social o total. Isso confirma que a gorjeta existe e é reconhecida — não confirma percentual nenhum. ⚠️ AUSENTE: percentual de gorjeta. Ensinar a mecânica (τον λογαριασμό, παρακαλώ, arredondar) e declarar que é costume variável. Não citar número.

steps.pt: Four money questions come up every single day here, and Greece answers three of them with an actual law.
First: taking your card is an obligation here, not a courtesy — written in law, tied to the trade's activity code.
Do you take card?

steps.promptPt: You are still in the doorway of a small place off the square, nothing ordered, wallet unopened. Settle it now. Speak now.
steps.pt: Do you take card?

steps.acao: The answer is usually yes here, and the sign at the door said so before you asked.
steps.pt: Of course, we take card.
The same law makes them post it. A card sign at the entrance and another at the till is part of the duty.

steps.promptPt: The little terminal behind the counter is face down and there is no sign anywhere on the glass. Check the one thing that decides your next ten minutes. Speak now.
steps.pt: Cash only?
Coverage runs by list, not by everything. Some very small trade sits outside it, so keep notes for the day it does.

steps.promptPt: Four of you ordered in waves over two hours and exactly one card is coming out. Get the figure before it does. Speak now.
steps.pt: How much is it all together?
That is the frame from B15, working at a table instead of a shelf. One opening, and the number arrives.

steps.promptPt: The plates were cleared twenty minutes ago, nobody is coming past, and you have a boat at six. Speak now.
steps.pt: The bill, please.
Second: cash stops at five hundred euros. At or above that figure the payment goes electronic, by card or transfer.

steps.promptPt: The total is well over what is in your wallet and three people are waiting behind you. Say how this ends. Speak now.
steps.pt: I'll pay by card.
Third, and this part is new. Since August 2025, taking money out where a community has a single machine costs nothing.

steps.promptPt: The only machine in the village wants you to agree to a screen of small print before it counts anything out, and the kiosk owner is standing right there. Speak now.
steps.pt: How much is the fee?

steps.acao: One fifty is the national ceiling for an independent operator. Above that figure, something is wrong with the screen, not with you.
steps.es: Ένα ευρώ και πενήντα, όπως παντού.
steps.pt: One euro fifty, like everywhere.
steps.tts: Ένα ευρώ και πενήντα, όπως παντού.

steps.pt: An independent operator cannot charge more than one euro fifty a withdrawal, anywhere in the country.

steps.promptPt: The kiosk owes you four euros back and everything in your hand is a fifty the machine just spat out. Speak now.
steps.pt: Do you have change?
You will see a domestic instant-payment app on till signs. It runs on Greek bank accounts, so it is not yours to use.

steps.promptPt: Two of you, two cards already out, one small tray in the middle of the table. Speak now.
steps.pt: Can we pay separately?

steps.acao: Yes arrives as an action, not as a word. He is already splitting it and printing twice.
steps.pt: Of course, separately. Two receipts.
Fourth: the tip. No institution publishes a percentage here, because there is no percentage to publish. Round up.

steps.promptPt: Long lunch, attentive service, and the coins have just landed on the saucer in front of you. Close it without arithmetic. Speak now.
steps.pt: Keep the change.
The printed receipt is the trader's legal duty, not a favour to you. Ask for it and it appears.

steps.promptPt: The terminal beeps, the drawer shuts, and nothing at all has printed. You want the paper for the hire-car claim. Speak now.
steps.pt: The receipt, please.

steps.es: Δέχεστε κάρτα; Πόσο κάνει όλα μαζί; Την απόδειξη, παρακαλώ.
steps.pinyin: DHE-he-ste KAR-ta · PO-so KA-ni O-la ma-ZI · tin a-PO-dhi-ksi pa-ra-ka-LO
steps.pt: Shadow the three sentences that settle almost any till in Greece.
steps.tts: Δέχεστε κάρτα; Πόσο κάνει όλα μαζί; Την απόδειξη, παρακαλώ.

steps.pt: I10 done, and GET THE GOOD STUFF with it. Card by law, cash to five hundred, and the machine fee has a ceiling.

aprofundar.titulo: Four money questions, three of them answered by law

secoes.titulo: The card is theirs to take, not to grant
secoes.corpo: Article 65 of law 4446/2016 imposes the acceptance of card payment — the duty is to accept, not merely to own a terminal — and article 66 makes the business say so visibly at the entrance and at the till. That is a stricter position than Italy or France, and a traveller arriving with the French habit of expecting a lawful minimum has the wrong expectation here. The limit worth knowing is where the duty comes from: it runs by ΚΑΔ, the activity code of the trade, and the code list was replaced by decision 119899/2023 (ΦΕΚ Β΄7115, 18.12.2023), which added 35 more codes covering open-air markets, food retail and kiosks. Wide, then, but a list rather than the whole of commerce.

secoes.titulo: IRIS is on the sign and is not for you
secoes.corpo: You will see IRIS advertised at tills all over the country: it is the domestic instant-payment scheme, compulsory across retail since November 2025. It settles between Greek bank accounts, which means a visiting card-holder normally cannot use it at all. This is worth knowing only so that the sign does not confuse you: what protects you at the counter is the card obligation, not the app.

secoes.titulo: Cash, its ceiling, and the machine that stopped charging
secoes.corpo: Cash to a business tops out at five hundred euros — article 69 §2 of law 4446/2016, down from the fifteen hundred that applied before — so an invoice at or above that figure goes electronic. And the withdrawal side changed recently in a way that matters on a small island: article 48 of law 5167/2024, as amended in July 2025 and in force since 11 August 2025, removes the commission on your own issuing bank's network, takes the fee to zero in a municipal community served by a single machine, and caps an independent operator at one euro fifty a withdrawal nationally. Carrying notes to a small island is still sensible — not every island has a machine at all — but the fee itself is no longer the thing to fear.

secoes.titulo: The tip has a tax rule and no percentage
secoes.corpo: Law 5162/2024 exempts up to three hundred euros a month per worker in tips from income tax, and the whole amount from social contributions, for sums paid from 1 November 2024. That is institutional confirmation that tipping happens and is recognised. It is not confirmation of a rate, and no ministry, federation or statistical office publishes one. So the mechanics are what you learn: ask for the bill, round the figure up, leave the coins. A calculated percentage is a habit imported from somewhere else.

permissao: You are allowed to ask how a place takes money before you order anything. Δέχεστε κάρτα; in the doorway is not suspicion and nobody reads it that way — it is thirty seconds of certainty bought before the bill exists, and the answer here is yes far more often than a visitor expects.
espelho: Anyone who has stood at a corner shop at home working out whether to break a big note or walk to a machine already knows this whole calculation. The only new part is that here most of it has been decided for you, in writing, by somebody else.

fichasCulturais.sinal: You put a card on the counter for a small purchase and hear μόνο μετρητά, with no sign anywhere explaining it.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: This is how it works here, and a visitor arguing about it would be the rude one.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: The duty in Greece is to accept card payment — article 65 of law 4446/2016 — and article 66 obliges the business to inform the customer visibly at the entrance and at the till. The scope is defined by activity code, and the code list was widened in December 2023 to take in open-air markets, food retail and kiosks. So a great many counters that say cash only are outside what the law allows.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Ask in the doorway rather than at the end. If the answer is cash only, decide there whether it is worth it, and go elsewhere or take out notes — you are choosing, not conceding.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You stop planning your day around cash you did not need, and you stop reading a lawful yes as a favour.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not a licence to lecture anyone at a counter, and not a claim of universal coverage: the legal criterion is the ΚΑΔ list, not all commerce, so some very small trades genuinely sit outside it. And IRIS, the app on the sign next to the till, settles between Greek bank accounts — it is not the thing protecting you.

fichasCulturais.sinal: The only cash machine in a village or on a small island puts a fee on the screen before it will release any notes.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: This is the price of being somewhere remote, and whatever number appears is what I have to accept.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: Article 48 of law 5167/2024, amended in July 2025 and in force since 11 August 2025, removed the commission on the issuing bank's own network, took the fee to zero in a municipal community served by a single machine, and set a national ceiling of one euro fifty per withdrawal by an independent operator. The remote village is precisely the case the rule was written for.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Read the figure on the screen before you confirm. Where there is one machine in the community, expect nothing; anywhere else, expect a small number and not a large one. Take out a sensible amount in one go rather than in three visits.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You stop treating the fee screen as a toll on being a foreigner and start reading it as information you can check.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not a promise about your own bank at home: currency conversion and your card issuer's own foreign-use charge are a separate contract and this law says nothing about them. Nor a promise that a machine exists — some small islands have none, and notes in your bag remain the sensible precaution.
